text: El Movimiento 19 de Abril, conocido por su acrónimo M-19 o simplemente «El Eme»,​​​ fue una guerrilla urbana colombiana,​ surgida después de las irregularidades en las elecciones presidenciales del 19 de abril de 1970, que dieron como ganador al oficialista del Frente Nacional Misael Pastrana Borrero sobre el candidato opositor: el expresidente y general Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, que derivaron de un supuesto fraude e…

title: 19 de enero En Bogotá Chester Allen Bitterman, asesor del Instituto Lingüístico de Verano, es secuestrado. El M-19 desvirtúa esta acción y califica como terrorista la acción.
text: Chester Allen "Chet" Bitterman III fue un lingüista y misionero cristiano estadounidense.

title: 4 de marzo, a través de la ley 37 de 1977, el Senado de la República aprobó la amnistía para los alzados en armas.
text: El Senado de la República es una de las dos cámaras del Congreso de la República de Colombia y una parte fundamental de la rama legislativa. El Senado de la República es un cuerpo colegiado de representación directa del pueblo y debe actuar consultando a la justicia y por el bien común.​ La composición y poderes del Senado se encuentran estipulados en el Título VI de la Constitución de Colombia de 1991​ y en la Le…

title: El M-19 asaltó Mocoa (Putumayo) capital de la Comisaría, dirigidos por Jaime Bateman
text: Jaime Alfonso Bateman Cayón, alias "El Flaco" o "Comandante Pablo", fue un político y guerrillero colombiano de ascendencia británica.

title: el mismo día en que se sancionó la ley de amnistía, el presidente Julio César Turbay anunció el rompimiento de relaciones diplomáticas con Cuba.
text: Julio César Turbay Ayala fue un político y diplomático colombiano de ascendencia libanesa. Fue presidente de Colombia entre el 7 de agosto de 1978 y el 7 de agosto de 1982.

title: 30 de abril: Operación Córdova. El Ejército Nacional liquida la columna guerrillera del M-19 que había desembarcado en Chocó hacía dos meses. Son abatidos 24 subversivos y capturados 30 más.
text: La Operación Cordova u Operación Choco fue un operativo del Ejército Nacional de Colombia, en contra de la guerrilla del Movimiento 19 de abril, desarrollado en 1982, en Choco.

title: Visita a Colombia de la Madre Teresa de Calcuta.
text: Teresa de Calcuta, de nombre secular Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu​ (AFI: ) y también conocida como Santa Teresa de Calcuta,​ Madre Teresa de Calcuta o Santa Madre Teresa de Calcuta, fue una monja católica de nacionalidad albanesa e india,​​​que fundó la congregación de las Misioneras de la Caridad en Calcuta en 1950. Durante más de 45 años atendió a pobres, enfermos, huérfanos y moribundos, al mismo tiempo que guiaba la…

title: 29 de junio Fabio Enrique Parra campeón de la Vuelta a Colombia 1981.
text: Fabio Enrique Parra Pinto es un ciclista colombiano, que hizo parte de la generación de la década de 1980 de su país que se destacó en las grandes vueltas europeas. Por su buen rendimiento en todos los terrenos, fue uno de los ciclistas colombianos que mejor se adaptó a la forma de correr en carreteras europeas.

title: El M-19 ataca con morteros la Casa de Nariño, sede presidencial en Bogotá.
text: La Casa de Nariño o Palacio de Nariño es la residencia oficial y principal sede de trabajo del presidente de la República de Colombia, ubicada en el centro histórico de la ciudad capital de Bogotá. El Palacio de Nariño o de la Carrera,​ fue inaugurado el 20 de julio de 1908 por el general Rafael Reyes y construido en los predios de la casa natal de Antonio Nariño.​ El diseño estuvo a cargo de los arquitectos Gastó…

title: Asesinado jefe seccional del Departamento Administrativo de Seguridad (DAS) en Medellín, mayor (r) Carlos Gustavo Monroy Arenas.
text: El Departamento Administrativo de Seguridad fue un organismo estatal encargado de realizar la inteligencia y contrainteligencia en Colombia. El 31 de octubre de 2011 el entonces presidente Juan Manuel Santos expidió el decreto 4057 mediante el cual suprimió esa entidad.

title: El diario El Espectador lanza la revista Los Monos creada y dirigida por Clara Helena Cano de Guerrero sobrina de Guillermo Cano Isaza que fue un suplemento dominical que salían todos los domingos, la revista estaba dedicada para los niños…
text: El Espectador es un periódico colombiano de circulación nacional. Fue fundado por Fidel Cano Gutiérrez el 22 de marzo de 1887​en Medellín.

title: Masacre en el Estadio Alfonso López de Bucaramanga.
text: Estadio Américo Montanini​ es un recinto deportivo situado en la ciudad colombiana de Bucaramanga. Cuenta con un aforo para 25 000 espectadores.​ Es la sede del Atlético Bucaramanga, club de la Categoría Primera A del fútbol profesional colombiano.

title: Guerrilleros del M-19 Secuestro del Curtiss C-46 de Aeropesca en Medellín, y lo cargan con armas en La Guajira. Finalmente lo hacen acuatizar en las selvas del sur.
text: El Secuestro del Curtiss C-46 de Aeropesca se registró el 21 de octubre de 1981 a una aeronave con matrícula HK-388, perteneciente a la empresa Aerovías de la Pesca y Colonización del Suroeste Colombiano (Aeropesca), cuando cubría una ruta desde el Aeropuerto Enrique Olaya Herrera de Medellín y procedía a dirigirse a realizar una escala en Barranquilla, luego irían a Bahía Solano y finalmente regresarían a Medellín.
wiki: Secuestro del Curtiss C-46 de Aeropesca

title: Hundimiento de El Karina, buque del M-19, cuando pretendía ingresar un poderoso arsenal por la costa Pacífica colombiana.
text: El Hundimiento de El Karina es el nombre con que se conoce a un combate marítimo en el que estuvieron involucrados la Armada de la República de Colombia, la Tercera Brigada del Ejército Nacional{{Cita requerida}} y el grupo guerrillero Movimiento 19 de abril, ocurrido el 14 de noviembre de 1981, en aguas continentales de la costa pacífica de Colombia.​​

title: Los narcotraficantes anuncian la conformación del Muerte a Secuestradores (MAS), como retaliación por el secuestro de Martha Nieves Ochoa. Lo integran 2000 hombres.
text: El MAS fue un grupo narcoparamilitar financiado por los carteles del narcotráfico en Colombia.​ Su función principal era proteger a los capos de la mafia, empresarios, políticos, militares y terratenientes de las acciones de las guerrillas como el Movimiento 19 de abril (M-19) las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia - Ejército del Pueblo (FARC-EP) llevando a cabo asesinatos selectivos a secuestradores, gue…

title: Independiente Medellín ganó la Copa Colombia al Deportivo Cali 3 a 1.
text: Deportivo Independiente Medellín, popularmente conocido por sus siglas como el DIM, es un club de fútbol de Colombia fundado bajo el nombre de «Medellín Football Club» el 14 de noviembre de 1913 por Alberto Uribe Piedrahíta.​ Pertenece a la ciudad de Medellín, capital del departamento de Antioquia. Actualmente juega en la Categoría Primera A del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano.

title: final del Campeonato colombiano 1981 Atlético Nacional Campeón ante América de Cali.
text: El Campeonato colombiano 1981 fue el trigésimo cuarto torneo de la primera división del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano en la historia. El campeón de esta edición fue el Atlético Nacional, que consiguió su cuarto título, y el subcampeón fue Deportes Tolima.

title: en la costa atlántica de Colombia, un Twin Otter de la aerolínea Aces que volaba entre Montería y Coveñas, se estrella en un cerro. El accidente deja un balance de once muertos.
text: Aces fue una aerolínea colombiana con sede en la Torre del Café en el centro Medellín, Colombia.​ Fue fundada en 1971 y liquidada en 2003 tras fusionarse con Avianca.​

title: Liga colombiana: Atlético Nacional, campeón.
text: La División Mayor del Fútbol Colombiano es una entidad deportiva que forma parte de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol y se encarga de organizar, administrar y reglamentar los torneos de fútbol profesional en Colombia: Primera A; Primera B; la Copa Colombia, la Superliga de Colombia y la Liga Femenina.

title: Canaguaro
text: Canaguaro es una película colombiana de 1981​ dirigida por el cineasta chileno Dunav Kuzmanich con la colaboración de Pepe Sánchez, que relata la situación vivida en los Llanos Orientales durante la época de La Violencia en Colombia, con una mirada crítica a la manipulación de la clase política y la situación social que alimentaría el conflicto armado en Colombia. Este filme es uno de los pocos dentro de la histor…

title: 27 horas con la muerte
text: 27 horas con la muerte es una película colombiana de 1981 de suspenso y terror, escrita y dirigida por Jairo Pinilla.

title: Erotikón
text: Erotikón es una película mexicana de 1981 dirigida y producida por Ramiro Meléndez y estrenada en septiembre de 1981. Protagonizada por Juan Antonio Edwards, Nelly Moreno, Álvaro Ruiz Zúñiga y Mariangela Giordano en los papeles principales.

title: La abuela
text: La abuela es una película dramática colombiana de 1981 dirigida por Leopoldo Pinzón con guion de Julio Jiménez. La trama sigue a una familia decadente y tradicional en Bogotá gobernada por una abuela dominante y despótica que solo ama a su nieto favorito.

title: Greece enters the European Economic Community, predecessor of the European Union.
text: The European Economic Community was a regional organisation created by the Treaty of Rome of 1957, aiming to foster economic integration among its member states. It was subsequently renamed the European Community (EC) upon becoming integrated into the first pillar of the newly formed European Union (EU) in 1993.

title: A funeral service is held in West Germany for Nazi Grand Admiral Karl Doenitz following his death on December 24.
text: Karl Dönitz was a German naval officer and politician who briefly succeeded Adolf Hitler as the head of state of Germany in the Nazi era after Hitler's suicide during the Second World War in April 1945. He held this position until the dissolution of the Flensburg Government, about two weeks after Germany's unconditional surrender to the Allies.

title: Salvadoran Civil War: The FMLN launches its first major offensive, gaining control of most of Morazán and Chalatenango departments.
text: The Salvadoran Civil War was a twelve-year civil war in El Salvador that was fought between the government of El Salvador that was backed by the United States, against the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN), a coalition of left-wing guerrilla groups that was backed by Cuba under Fidel Castro, Daniel Ortega's Nicaragua and the Soviet Union. A coup on 15 October 1979 followed by government killings of …

title: Pope John Paul II receives a delegation led by Polish Solidarity leader Lech Wałęsa at the Vatican.
text: Pope John Paul II was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 16 October 1978 until his death in 2005. He was the first non-Italian pope since Adrian VI in the 16th century, as well as the third longest-serving pope in history, after St.

title: Iran releases the 52 Americans held for 444 days, minutes after Ronald Reagan is sworn in as the 40th President of the United States, ending the Iran hostage crisis.
text: Ronald Wilson Reagan was an American politician and actor who served as the 40th president of the United States from 1981 to 1989. A member of the Republican Party, he became an important figure in the American conservative movement.

title: The first DeLorean automobile, a stainless steel sports car with gull-wing doors, rolls off the production line in Dunmurry, Northern Ireland.
text: The DMC DeLorean is a rear-engine, two-seat sports car manufactured and marketed by John DeLorean's DeLorean Motor Company for the American market from 1981 until 1983—ultimately the only car brought to market by the fledgling company. The DeLorean is sometimes referred to by its internal pre-production designation, DMC-12, although this was not used in sales or marketing materials for the production model.

title: An earthquake of .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Ms 6.8 magnitude in Sichuan, China, kills 150 people. Japan suffers a less serious earthquake on the same day.
text: The 1981 Dawu earthquake occurred on 24 January at 5:13 a.m. CST, in Sichuan, China.

title: In South Africa the largest part of the town Laingsburg is swept away within minutes by one of the strongest floods ever experienced in the Great Karoo.
text: Laingsburg is a town located in the Western Cape province in South Africa. It is a relatively large agricultural town in the semi-arid Great Karoo; its economy is based on farming goats, sheep, fruits, and vegetable.

title: The Indonesian passenger ship Tampomas II catches fire and capsizes in the Java Sea, killing 580 people.
text: The Java Sea is an extensive shallow sea in Indonesia. It lies on the Sunda Shelf, between the islands of Borneo to the north, Java to the south, Sumatra to the west, and Sulawesi to the east.

title: Gro Harlem Brundtland becomes Prime Minister of Norway.
text: Gro Brundtland, known as Gro Harlem Brundtland, is a Norwegian stateswoman and former physician, who thrice served as the Prime Minister of Norway (1981, 1986–1989, and 1990–1996), and as the leader of the Labour Party from 1981 to 1992, and as the director-general of the World Health Organization from 1998 to 2003. She is also known for having chaired the Brundtland Commission which presented the Brundtland Repor…

title: In Greece, 20 fans of Olympiacos F.C. and 1 fan of AEK Athens die, while 54 are injured, after a stampede at the Karaiskakis Stadium in Piraeus, possibly because Gate 7 does not open immediately after the end of the game.
text: The Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium, commonly referred to as the Karaiskakis Stadium (Greek: Στάδιο Καραϊσκάκη, ), and also known as “Bombonera”, is a football stadium in Piraeus, Attica, Greece, and the home ground of the Piraeus football club Olympiacos. It is named after Georgios Karaiskakis, a military commander and national hero of the Greek War of Independence, who was mortally wounded in the area.

title: Polish Prime Minister Józef Pińkowski resigns and is replaced by General Wojciech Jaruzelski.
text: Józef Pińkowski was a Polish Communist politician and economist who served as 35th Prime Minister of Poland from 1980 to 1981.

title: Stardust fire: A fire at the Stardust nightclub in Artane, Dublin, Ireland, in the early hours kills 48 young people and injures 214. In 2024 these will be declared as unlawful killings.
text: The Stardust fire was a fatal fire at the Stardust nightclub in Artane, Dublin, Ireland, in the early hours of 14 February 1981. More than 800 people were attending a disco there, of whom 48 died, and 214 were injured as a result of the fire; in later years suicides of survivors and family members were also linked to the event.

title: 1981 Spanish coup d'état attempt ("23-F"): Antonio Tejero, with members of the Guardia Civil, enters the Spanish Congress of Deputies and stops the session where Leopoldo Calvo-Sotelo is about to be named president of the government. The…
text: A coup d'état was attempted in Spain in February 1981 by right-wing, Francoist elements of the Civil Guard and the Spanish military. The failure of the coup marked the last serious attempt to revert Spain to a Francoist state and served to consolidate Spain's democratization process.

title: A powerful Ms 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Athens, killing 22 people, injuring 400 people and destroying several buildings and 4,000 houses, mostly in Corinth and the nearby towns of Loutraki, Kiato and Xylokastro.
text: Kiato is a town in the northern part of Corinthia in the Peloponnese, Greece. It is the seat of the municipality of Sikyona.

title: 1981 Irish hunger strike: Bobby Sands, a Provisional Irish Republican Army member, begins a hunger strike for political status at HM Prison Maze (Long Kesh) in Northern Ireland, dying on May 5, the first of 7 IRA and 3 INLA hunger strikers…
text: A five-year protest during the Troubles by Irish republican prisoners in Northern Ireland culminated in a hunger strike in 1981. The protest began as the blanket protest in 1976 when the British government withdrew Special Category Status for convicted paramilitary prisoners.

title: Chilean military dictator Augusto Pinochet is sworn in as President of Chile for another 8-year term.
text: Augusto José Ramón Pinochet Ugarte was a Chilean army officer and military dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990. He led the Chilean Army in the overthrow of President Salvador Allende in 1973 and established a military junta.

title: In Italy, the Propaganda Due Masonic lodge is discovered.
text: A Masonic lodge is the basic organisational unit of Freemasonry. It is also a commonly used term for a building where Freemasons meet and hold their meetings.

title: Two or three workers are killed and four are injured during a ground test of Space Shuttle Columbia at Kennedy Space Center in the United States.
text: Space Shuttle Columbia was a Space Shuttle orbiter manufactured by Rockwell International and operated by NASA. Named after the first American ship to circumnavigate the globe, and the female personification of the United States, Columbia was the first of five Space Shuttle orbiters to fly in space, debuting the Space Shuttle launch vehicle on its maiden flight on April 12, 1981 and becoming the first spacecraft t…

title: The first London Marathon starts, with 7,500 runners.
text: The London Marathon is an annual marathon held in London, England. Founded by athletes Chris Brasher and John Disley in 1981, it is typically held in April, although it moved to October for 2020, 2021, and 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan: U.S. President Ronald Reagan is shot in the chest outside a Washington, D.C., hotel by John Hinckley Jr.; two police officers and Press Secretary James Brady are also wounded.
text: On March 30, 1981, Ronald Reagan, the president of the United States, was shot and wounded by John Hinckley Jr. outside of the Washington Hilton in Washington, D.C., as Reagan was returning to his limousine after a speaking engagement at the hotel.

title: Pantanal Matogrossense National Park designated in Brazil.
text: The Pantanal Matogrossense National Park is a national park in the state of Mato Grosso at the border to Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.

title: Publication of Stephen Jay Gould's critique of biological determinism, The Mismeasure of Man, in the United States.
text: Stephen Jay Gould was an American paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, historian of science, and one of the most widely read authors of popular science of his generation. Gould spent most of his career teaching at Harvard University and working at the American Museum of Natural History in New York.

title: The burning of Jaffna Public Library in Sri Lanka is begun by a mob of police and government-sponsored paramilitaries. They destroy over 97,000 volumes in one of the worst examples of ethnic book burning in the modern era.
text: A paramilitary is an armed, militarized-like force or unit that functions and is organized in a manner analogous to a military force, but does not have professional or legitimate status. The Oxford English Dictionary traces the use of the term "paramilitary" as far back as 1934.

title: Sefer ve Sefel opens as an English used bookstore in Jerusalem.
text: Sefer ve Sefel is an English-language secondhand bookshop in downtown Jerusalem, Israel. It was established in 1981 as the first combination bookshop/coffee shop in the country.

title: John Gardner successfully revives the James Bond novel series originated by Ian Fleming with Licence Renewed (not counting a faux biography of Bond and a pair of film novelizations, the first original Bond novel since 1968's Colonel Sun).…
text: Ian Lancaster Fleming was a British writer best known for his postwar James Bond series of spy novels. Fleming came from a wealthy family connected to the merchant bank Robert Fleming & Co., and his father Valentine Fleming was the Member of Parliament for Henley from 1910 until his death on the Western Front in 1917.

title: Colin MacCabe is denied tenure at the University of Cambridge, apparently because of a dispute within the English Faculty about the teaching of structuralism.
text: Colin Myles Joseph MacCabe is an English academic, literary critic, film scholar, author, and film producer. He is currently a distinguished professor of English and film at the University of Pittsburgh.

title: The PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction is given for the first time.
text: The PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction is awarded annually by the PEN/Faulkner Foundation to the authors of the year's best works of fiction by living Americans, Green Card holders or permanent residents. The winner receives US$15,000 and each of four runners-up receives US$5000.

title: Picasso's painting Guernica is returned from New York to Madrid.
text: Pablo Ruiz Picasso was a Spanish painter and sculptor who spent most of his adult life in France. One of the most influential artists of the 20th century, he is known for co-founding the Cubist movement, the invention of constructed sculpture, the co-invention of collage, and for the wide variety of styles that he helped develop and explore.

title: unknown date – Blek le Rat begins his stencil graffiti art in Paris.
text: Blek le Rat is a French graffiti artist. He was one of the first graffiti artists in Paris, and has been described as the "Father of stencil graffiti".
